claims.text: Adding approximately 3–5 at% Al and aging the alloy at about 850°C for 1–2 hours will induce nanoscale precipitates in a Ti- and Ni-primary high-entropy alloy.
The induced precipitates will be coherent and uniformly distributed in the matrix.
The precipitates may be Ni3Al or TiAl-based phases.
Nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Precipitation strengthening will increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
Precipitation strengthening will improve creep resistance at elevated temperature.
The Al-modified and aged alloy will have roughly 10–20% greater elevated-temperature yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified and aged alloy will have a lower creep rate than the baseline alloy.
The proposed precipitates are expected to remain stable during mechanical testing around 900°C.
The intervention is intended for alloys having at least five elements, with every element maintained between 5 and 35 at% and Ti and Ni as primary constituents.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on precipitate coherence and spatial distribution.
Changes in processing parameters may alter precipitate coherence and distribution.
Al addition may cause detrimental phase formation instead of the intended precipitate population.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits 3–5 at% Al, but the stated compositional boundary requires every element to be present at 5–35 at%; any Al level below 5 at% violates that boundary.
